05: Converting Overlaps to Lines

Now let's see how the ProjectionGenerator orchestrates all the pieces we've learned about into a cohesive pipeline, and how overlaps are converted into the final visible and hidden line geometry.

The Main Classes

Class Responsibility File
ProjectionGenerator Main orchestrator - coordinates entire pipeline src/ProjectionGenerator.js
EdgeGenerator Extracts hard/silhouette edges and intersection edges src/EdgeGenerator.js
ProjectedEdgeCollector Clips edges against meshes, generates output geometry src/ProjectionGenerator.js
LineObjectsBVH BVH structure optimized for line segments src/utils/LineObjectsBVH.js
VisibilityCuller GPU-based pre-filtering of visible meshes src/VisibilityCuller.js

Basic Usage

import { ProjectionGenerator } from 'three-edge-projection';

// Create generator with settings
const generator = new ProjectionGenerator();
generator.angleThreshold = 50;              // degrees for hard edges
generator.includeIntersectionEdges = true; // detect overlapping geometry
generator.iterationTime = 30;              // ms per iteration (for UI responsiveness)

// Generate edges (async version)
const result = await generator.generateAsync(scene);

// Get output geometries
const visibleLines = result.getVisibleLineGeometry();
const hiddenLines = result.getHiddenLineGeometry();

// Create line segments for rendering
const visibleMesh = new THREE.LineSegments(visibleLines, solidMaterial);
const hiddenMesh = new THREE.LineSegments(hiddenLines, dashedMaterial);

The Generator Pattern

All core functions use JavaScript generators (function*). This allows the processing to yield periodically, keeping the UI responsive during long operations. 

// The generate() function is a generator
*generate(scene, options) {
    // Step 1: Generate candidate edges
    yield* edgeGenerator.getEdgesGenerator(scene, edges);

    // Step 2: Generate intersection edges (optional)
    if (includeIntersectionEdges) {
        yield* edgeGenerator.getIntersectionEdgesGenerator(scene, edges);
    }

    // Step 3: Pre-filter degenerate edges
    edges = edges.filter(e => !isYProjectedLineDegenerate(e));
    yield;

    // Steps 4-5: Build BVH, compute overlaps, convert to lines
    yield* collector.addEdgesGenerator(edges);

    return collector;
}

// The generateAsync() wrapper runs the generator with requestAnimationFrame
generateAsync(scene, options) {
    return new Promise((resolve) => {
        const task = this.generate(scene, options);

        function run() {
            const result = task.next();
            if (result.done) {
                resolve(result.value);
            } else {
                requestAnimationFrame(run);
            }
        }

        run();
    });
}

Why Generators?

Without generators, processing a complex model would freeze the browser for seconds or even minutes. With generators:

  • Each step can yield after ~30ms of work
  • The browser can process events and update the UI between yields
  • You can show progress indicators to the user
  • Processing can be cancelled via AbortSignal

Progress Tracking

You can monitor progress using the onProgress callback: 

const result = await generator.generateAsync(scene, {
    onProgress: (stage, progress, collector) => {
        console.log(`${stage}: ${(progress * 100).toFixed(1)}%`);

        // During BVH processing, you can preview partial results:
        if (collector && stage === 'Building BVH & computing overlaps') {
            previewMesh.geometry = collector.getVisibleLineGeometry();
        }
    }
});

Cancellation

Use an AbortSignal to cancel long-running operations: 

const controller = new AbortController();

// Start generation
const promise = generator.generateAsync(scene, {
    signal: controller.signal
});

// Cancel if user clicks a button
cancelButton.addEventListener('click', () => {
    controller.abort();
});

try {
    const result = await promise;
} catch (error) {
    if (error.message.includes('aborted')) {
        console.log('Generation cancelled');
    }
}

Performance Tips

Typical Time Distribution

Visibility culling: ~4% Generating candidate edges: ~1% Pre-filtering edges: ~0.1% Building BVH & overlaps: ~95% ← THE BOTTLENECK

The BVH and overlap computation dominates because it must check every edge against every potentially-occluding triangle.

Optimization Strategies

Strategy How Impact
Use VisibilityCuller Pre-filter to only visible meshes Can skip 50-90% of geometry
Reduce mesh complexity Simplify models before processing Linear reduction in time
Disable intersection edges includeIntersectionEdges = false Skip ~1-5% of total time
Increase angle threshold Higher threshold = fewer edges Fewer edges to clip
Pre-compute BVH Set geometry.boundsTree Skip BVH build time

Using VisibilityCuller

import { ProjectionGenerator, VisibilityCuller } from 'three-edge-projection';

// Create culler (needs a WebGLRenderer)
const culler = new VisibilityCuller();
culler.resolution = 512;  // Higher = more accurate, slower

// Pass to generator
const result = await generator.generateAsync(scene, {
    visibilityCuller: culler
});

Congratulations!

You now understand the complete edge projection pipeline! From extracting edges based on face angles and silhouettes, through finding intersection edges, to the complex occlusion clipping algorithm that determines visibility.

Key takeaways:

  • BVH acceleration is crucial for performance
  • The generator pattern keeps UI responsive
  • Clipping is the bottleneck - optimize there first
  • The output is two BufferGeometries: visible and hidden lines
